project.name: scrutinizer-electron
project.description: Foveated vision simulator — Electron + WebGL 2.0 + WebGPU compute. Renders any web page through a three-stage model of human peripheral vision (LGN/V1/V4) bound to the mouse cursor.

nodes.name: complexity-hud.js
nodes.summary: Draggable on-screen HUD that visualizes per-frame visual complexity scores, regional crowding/edge stats, and pipeline performance metrics across tabbed views.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE-wrapped UMD class (ComplexityHUD) attached to window; tab-based DOM construction with inline styles.

nodes.name: ComplexityHUD
nodes.summary: Encapsulates the complexity HUD: builds the tabbed DOM, handles drag/hover, and rerenders score, stats, spatial heatmap, and performance panels on update.

nodes.name: gaze-model.js
nodes.summary: Tracks pointer-driven gaze position with velocity smoothing and optional scanpath playback, feeding the foveated render loop a stable gaze point and scalar velocity.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE-wrapped GazeModel class; defensive isFinite guards on incoming pointer coordinates.

nodes.name: GazeModel
nodes.summary: Maintains gaze position, velocity, and zoom-aware coordinate mapping; integrates pointer input and optional scanpath playback.

nodes.name: logger.js
nodes.summary: Tiny logging facade exporting log/info/warn/error helpers used across the renderer to centralize console output.

nodes.name: scrutinizer.js
nodes.summary: Top-level renderer orchestrator that wires gaze, content analysis, WebGL/WebGPU pipelines, SVG overlay, visual memory, and IPC into a single render loop and command surface for the Electron app.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE-wrapped Scrutinizer class; integrates Electron ipcRenderer and dynamically requires shared/modes.json at runtime.

nodes.name: Scrutinizer
nodes.summary: Central renderer controller: initializes WebGPU with WebGL fallback, manages frame submission, debug toggles, scanpath playback, and mode/setting IPC handlers.

nodes.name: svg-overlay.js
nodes.summary: Manages the SVG layer rendered above the WebGL canvas, drawing fovea/parafovea rings, comfort guides, tick marks, optional grid, and the mouse cursor indicator.

nodes.name: SVGOverlay
nodes.summary: Builds and updates SVG overlay groups (fovea ring with tick pool, parafovea, comfort guide, optional grid, mouse cursor) in response to gaze and mode changes.

nodes.name: visual-memory.js
nodes.summary: Tracks where the gaze has dwelled to produce a fading memory mask used for inhibition-of-return shading in the foveated render.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE-wrapped VisualMemory class with canvas-backed mask plus typed-array decay.

nodes.name: VisualMemory
nodes.summary: Records visited gaze locations into a decaying canvas mask, exposes update/reset/renderMask for the IoR overlay path, and supports configurable memory limits.

nodes.name: webgl-renderer.js
nodes.summary: WebGL 2.0 foveated rendering pipeline: compiles GLSL programs, manages textures, uploads frame/mask/compute outputs, and dispatches the multi-stage LGN/V1/V4 render passes.
nodes.languageNotes: IIFE-wrapped WebGLRenderer class with extensive GLSL program/uniform setup.

nodes.name: WebGLRenderer
nodes.summary: Owns the GL2 context and shader programs powering the foveated visual simulator, including texture uploads, compute-result blending, and per-frame parameter binding.

nodes.name: webgpu-crowding-compute.js
nodes.summary: WebGPU compute pipeline that estimates eccentricity-dependent visual crowding from the input frame, feeding modulation back into the WebGL render path.

nodes.name: WebGPUCrowdingCompute
nodes.summary: Allocates WebGPU bind groups and buffers for the crowding compute shader, dispatches per-frame work, and provides readback of the resulting modulation map.

nodes.name: webgpu-probe.js
nodes.summary: Probes the host for a usable WebGPU adapter/device and reports limits used to pick between Tier-16 and higher-tier compute paths.

nodes.name: probeWebGPU
nodes.summary: Async probe that requests a WebGPU adapter and device, captures limits/features, and returns a result describing whether the pyramid compute path is viable.

nodes.name: webgpu-pyramid-compute.js
nodes.summary: WebGPU pyramid (multi-scale) compute pipeline implementing the foveated pooling stack with WGSL shaders, buffer pools, and readback paths consumed by the renderer.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest WebGPU module in the renderer; manages WGSL compilation and tier-aware pipeline selection.

nodes.name: WebGPUPyramidCompute
nodes.summary: Manages the multi-tier WebGPU pyramid compute pipeline: shader compilation, bind groups, dispatch sequencing, dynamic resize, and async readback of the pooled output.

nodes.name: webgpu-safety.js
nodes.summary: Lightweight harness that watches WebGPU device-lost events and exposes an isAlive guard so the renderer can fall back to a CPU/WebGL tier safely.

nodes.name: WebGPUSafetyHarness
nodes.summary: Tracks device-lost state on a WebGPU GPUDevice and surfaces an isAlive flag plus reset hook used by the render loop's fallback path.

nodes.name: visual-memory.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest unit tests for VisualMemory, exercising mask decay, limit changes, reset semantics, and inhibition-of-return mode behavior against a mocked canvas context.

nodes.name: analyze-artifacts.js
nodes.summary: Post-capture quality checker that scans rendered PNGs for chromatic shift and peripheral fog by computing Oklab chroma and patch standard-deviation contrast around the fixation point.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements sRGB-to-Oklab color conversion in pure JS for perceptually uniform chroma comparisons.

nodes.name: rgbToOklab
nodes.summary: Converts an sRGB triplet to Oklab L/a/b using the standard linear-RGB to LMS matrix and cube-root response.

nodes.name: samplePatch
nodes.summary: Averages Oklab values across a square patch of a PNG around a given pixel center.

nodes.name: patchStdDev
nodes.summary: Computes the Oklab-L standard deviation of a square patch, used as a local contrast proxy.

nodes.name: checkColorShift
nodes.summary: Samples patches at increasing eccentricities and reports the maximum chroma drift versus the fixation patch to detect peripheral color tinting.

nodes.name: checkFog
nodes.summary: Measures local contrast in the periphery and compares it to the fovea to detect washed-out (fog) rendering artifacts.

nodes.name: analyzeArtifacts
nodes.summary: Public entrypoint that runs all artifact checks against a capture directory and aggregates pass/fail results.

nodes.name: capture-compute-texture.js
nodes.summary: Headless capture driver that exercises the WebGPU compute-texture rendering path and dumps raw PNGs for inspection.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Ensures the output directory exists, runs the capture batch through the shared runner, and prints a summary of resulting raw files.

nodes.name: capture-crowding-tier3.js
nodes.summary: Headless capture driver for Tier-3 crowding test specs, generating PNGs that probe Bouma-spacing and pyramid-blend behavior.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Builds the Tier-3 crowding spec list and dispatches it to the capture runner, reporting raw outputs and exiting with a status code.

nodes.name: capture-golden.js
nodes.summary: Headless capture driver that generates the canonical golden image set across pages, modes, and fixations for visual regression baselines.

nodes.name: buildSpecs
nodes.summary: Enumerates the full Cartesian product of pages, modes, and fixations into capture spec objects for the golden baseline set.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Prepares output directory, builds the golden spec list, runs the capture pipeline, and prints summary plus exit status.

nodes.name: capture-isotropic-comparison.js
nodes.summary: Headless capture driver that renders matched pages under isotropic versus foveated modes to support side-by-side comparison panels.

nodes.name: buildSpecs
nodes.summary: Constructs capture spec list pairing each page with every mode and fixation for isotropic comparison rendering.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Prints run parameters, ensures output dir, and dispatches isotropic comparison specs to the capture runner.

nodes.name: capture-mode-comparison.js
nodes.summary: Headless capture driver that renders the same pages across every Scrutinizer mode and stamps outputs with the app version for change-tracking.

nodes.name: buildSpecs
nodes.summary: Constructs capture spec list for each (page, mode) combination used in the mode comparison sweep.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Reads app version from package.json, builds version-tagged output dir, runs the mode comparison capture set, and copies a 'latest' alias.

nodes.name: capture-pyramid-subbands.js
nodes.summary: Headless capture driver that generates per-subband Gaussian pyramid PNGs for a reference image to validate the multi-resolution pipeline.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses CLI source argument, runs capture specs through the shared runner, and post-processes a reference pyramid for comparison.

nodes.name: generateReferencePyramid
nodes.summary: Builds a Gaussian/Laplacian reference pyramid in pure JS by repeatedly downsampling and upsampling a PNG, writing each band to disk.

nodes.name: downsample
nodes.summary: Halves image resolution via 2x2 box-filter averaging across all four RGBA channels.

nodes.name: upsample
nodes.summary: Nearest-neighbor upsamples an image to a target width and height for pyramid band reconstruction.

nodes.name: writeBandPng
nodes.summary: Clamps and encodes an RGBA buffer to a PNG file for a single pyramid band.

nodes.name: capture-raw-electron.js
nodes.summary: Headless capture driver that produces raw unprocessed Electron screenshots and emits a manifest of dimensions for downstream analysis.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs the raw Electron capture set and writes a manifest.json describing the output PNG sizes for each page.

nodes.name: capture-smoke.js
nodes.summary: Smoke-test capture script that runs a small representative capture set and immediately validates outputs via the artifact analyzer, exiting non-zero on regression.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a smoke capture run, invokes analyzeArtifacts for chroma/fog checks, and propagates failures as a non-zero exit for CI gating.

nodes.name: capture-temporal-variance.js
nodes.summary: Headless capture driver that takes repeated shots of the same scene to measure frame-to-frame temporal variance in foveated rendering.

nodes.name: buildSpecs
nodes.summary: Generates N repeat-capture specs per page/mode/fixation combination for the temporal variance experiment.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Builds the repeat-capture matrix, writes a spec sidecar manifest, runs the captures, and reports summary statistics.

nodes.name: capture-manifest.js
nodes.summary: Capture manifest library that hashes capture specs, persists per-output metadata, and decides whether a capture can be skipped because nothing relevant changed.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses SHA-256 hashing of canonicalized JSON to produce stable spec fingerprints.

nodes.name: specHash
nodes.summary: Computes a 16-char SHA-256 fingerprint of a capture spec after canonicalizing key order.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads and parses the manifest.json sidecar for an output directory, returning an empty manifest on miss or parse error.

nodes.name: shouldSkip
nodes.summary: Returns true when the existing output file matches the spec hash and app version recorded in the manifest, enabling incremental capture runs.

nodes.name: recordCapture
nodes.summary: Records the spec hash, app version, and timestamp for a newly captured output into the manifest sidecar.

nodes.name: capture-runner.js
nodes.summary: Shared capture runner that groups capture specs, skips unchanged outputs via the manifest, and spawns Electron child processes in batches with retry-on-batch-failure fallback.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements per-group fallback: failed batch jobs are retried one-by-one before being marked failed.

nodes.name: groupKey
nodes.summary: Derives a stable group key from a capture spec, used to batch shots that can share a single Electron launch.

nodes.name: runBatch
nodes.summary: Writes a temp spec file and spawns the Electron capture child process for a batch of shots, resolving with results or rejecting on non-zero exit.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Public entrypoint that filters specs via manifest, groups them by Electron launch parameters, runs each batch, and falls back to per-spec retries on batch failure.

nodes.name: analyzer.js
nodes.summary: CLI helper that decodes a PNG buffer, downscales it, and runs the Oklab-based congestion analysis pipeline to produce composite scores and a heatmap PNG.

nodes.name: downscale
nodes.summary: Performs nearest-neighbor downscaling of RGBA pixel data while preserving aspect ratio, capping output dimensions at maxDim.

nodes.name: analyzePixels
nodes.summary: Converts sRGB pixels to Oklab, computes per-channel local variance (luminance and chroma), edge density, and a composite congestion rating with timing metadata.

nodes.name: analyzePng
nodes.summary: Decodes a PNG buffer via pngjs and forwards its pixels to the analyzer.

nodes.name: saveHeatmapPng
nodes.summary: Encodes a normalized float feature map into an 8-bit grayscale PNG buffer for visualization.

nodes.name: server.js
nodes.summary: Model Context Protocol server exposing Playwright-driven page-capture-and-analyze tools so an LLM agent can score visual congestion of live URLs.
nodes.languageNotes: Node CommonJS server using @modelcontextprotocol/sdk over stdio transport; orchestrates Playwright captures plus the analyzer pipeline.

nodes.name: captureAndAnalyze
nodes.summary: Opens a Playwright context, navigates to a URL with optional viewport and scroll, captures a screenshot, and runs analyzePng to return rounded congestion metrics.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that connects the MCP server to the stdio transport and surfaces fatal errors.

nodes.name: congestion-core.js
nodes.summary: Pure-JS implementation of Feature Congestion (separable Gaussian blur, local variance, Sobel-like edge density, normalization, and composite scoring) used by both renderer and CLI tooling.
nodes.languageNotes: Separable 1D Gaussian kernels with clamped edges; Welford-style variance accumulation via blur-of-square minus square-of-blur.

nodes.name: generateGaussianKernel
nodes.summary: Builds a normalized 1D Gaussian kernel of radius 3 sigma.

nodes.name: blurHorizontal
nodes.summary: Applies a 1D Gaussian kernel along rows with clamped boundary handling.

nodes.name: blurVertical
nodes.summary: Applies a 1D Gaussian kernel along columns with clamped boundary handling.

nodes.name: gaussianBlur
nodes.summary: Separable 2D Gaussian blur driver that allocates kernels and chains horizontal then vertical passes.

nodes.name: computeLocalVariance
nodes.summary: Computes local variance per pixel as E[x^2] - E[x]^2 using two Gaussian blurs over the channel and its square.

nodes.name: normalizeFeature
nodes.summary: Rescales a feature map to [0,1] using its min/max range.

nodes.name: computeStats
nodes.summary: Computes mean, std, and percentile statistics (p50, p90, p95, p99) over a feature map by sorting a float copy.

nodes.name: computeEdgeDensity
nodes.summary: Computes edge-density feature map via finite-difference gradient magnitude with optional Gaussian smoothing of the result.

nodes.name: computeCompositeScore
nodes.summary: Combines congestion and edge-density statistics into a 0-100 composite score plus a human-readable rating tier.

nodes.name: image-processor.js
nodes.summary: ImageProcessor class providing Oklab-based desaturation (with rod-sensitive luminance lift), Gaussian pyramid construction, separable box blurs, radial blending, and foveal masking for the WebGL fallback / 2D-canvas pipeline.

nodes.name: ImageProcessor
nodes.summary: Canvas-side image manipulation toolkit: rod-sensitive desaturation, multi-level blur pyramids, separable box blur, radial blending, and foveal mask rendering.

nodes.name: oklab-utils.js
nodes.summary: Pure-JS Oklab color-space utilities: sRGB linearization, forward and inverse Oklab transforms, and a desaturation helper using Oklab chroma scaling.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the standard Bjorn Ottosson Oklab matrix transforms with cube-root nonlinearity.

nodes.name: linearSrgbToOklab
nodes.summary: Converts linear sRGB to Oklab via LMS-cube-root pipeline.

nodes.name: oklabToLinearSrgb
nodes.summary: Inverse Oklab transform back to linear sRGB.

nodes.name: compare-crowding-modes.js
nodes.summary: Validation script that compares golden PNG captures between two crowding-mode renderings (mode 0 vs mode 10), measuring cyan-cluster spread, patch-level luminance/chroma variance, and eccentricity gradients, then writes a markdown comparison report.

nodes.name: findGoldenDir
nodes.summary: Resolves the most recent versioned golden capture directory under tests/golden, optionally overridden by --version.

nodes.name: detectFixationY
nodes.summary: Locates the vertical fixation band in a capture by clustering rows that contain cyan annotation pixels.

nodes.name: findCyanClusters
nodes.summary: Scans a bounded region of a PNG for cyan pixels and groups them into horizontal clusters approximating rendered letter positions.

nodes.name: analyzePng
nodes.summary: For each eccentricity x direction, samples target and flanker bands and computes per-condition cyan counts and spread ratios used to quantify crowding.

nodes.name: analyzePatches
nodes.summary: Compares Oklab luminance and chroma variance in matched patches between two captures to detect texture metamer differences across crowding modes.

nodes.name: sampleOklabPatch
nodes.summary: Samples a rectangular patch from a PNG and returns parallel arrays of Oklab L, a, b values.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full comparison: discovers captures, runs analyzers across eccentricities and font sizes, prints summary tables, and writes a timestamped markdown report.

nodes.name: checkGradient
nodes.summary: Verifies that crowding ratios increase monotonically across eccentricity tiers (3,6,10 deg) as a sanity check.

nodes.name: export-saliency.js
nodes.summary: Headless CLI that computes color, edge-density, and feature-congestion saliency maps for one or many PNGs and writes per-coordinate samples plus aggregate JSON for downstream analysis.

nodes.name: computeCenterSurround
nodes.summary: Implements a simple Itti-Koch center-surround difference by subtracting two Gaussian blurs at different scales.

nodes.name: computeSaliencyMaps
nodes.summary: Builds Oklab-based color, edge-density, and congestion feature maps from raw pixels and returns combined saliency plus stats.

nodes.name: sampleAtCoordinate
nodes.summary: Samples a radial neighborhood around a source-image (x,y) coordinate from a downscaled feature map and returns mean/max statistics.

nodes.name: processImage
nodes.summary: Loads a PNG, computes its saliency maps, then samples each requested coordinate against the selected metrics, returning rounded numeric results.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that dispatches between single-image and batch-directory modes and writes JSON results to disk.

nodes.name: extract-congestion.js
nodes.summary: Batch script that downscales images, computes congestion and edge-density maps at a configurable sigma, saves heatmap PNGs, and emits a JSON manifest of per-image stats.

nodes.name: downscale
nodes.summary: Nearest-neighbor downscale of a parsed PNG to a maximum dimension, returning width/height/pixels.

nodes.name: computeCongestion
nodes.summary: Runs the full Oklab-based congestion pipeline on a downscaled image and returns congestion and edge-density maps plus composite scoring stats.

nodes.name: saveHeatmap
nodes.summary: Writes a normalized float feature map to disk as an 8-bit grayscale PNG.

nodes.name: collectImages
nodes.summary: Gathers candidate PNGs from the Rosenholtz reference set and the local screenshots directory into a unified list.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that iterates collected images, runs congestion at requested sigmas, writes heatmaps, and persists a summary JSON manifest.

nodes.name: content-analysis.js
nodes.summary: Coordinator for DOM-aware perception: owns saliency/congestion Web Workers, manages structure/primitive/meta canvases, and orchestrates Gestalt clustering to upload texture maps to the WebGL renderer.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy reliance on createImageBitmap + Worker.postMessage for async saliency/congestion compute; double-buffered smoothing canvases for temporal stability.

nodes.name: _initSaliencyWorker
nodes.summary: Spawns the saliency Web Worker, wires up message handling, and prepares the target canvas to receive smoothed saliency maps.

nodes.name: _initCongestionWorker
nodes.summary: Spawns the feature congestion Web Worker and binds its result frames to the smoothing canvas for V1 clutter modulation.

nodes.name: submitForCongestion
nodes.summary: Checksums an incoming frame to skip duplicates, then posts the ImageBitmap to the congestion worker for clutter analysis.

nodes.name: submitFrameForSaliency
nodes.summary: Submits a frame to the saliency worker after checksum deduplication, logging cadence for diagnostics.

nodes.name: handleStructureUpdate
nodes.summary: Core DOM-aware draw-order routine: receives DOM block list, runs Gestalt clustering, sorts text-bearing vs non-text-bearing primitives, paints structure/primitive/meta canvases, and uploads all three textures to the WebGL renderer.

nodes.name: renderStructureAnnotations
nodes.summary: Builds DOM overlay annotations visualizing detected structure blocks for the debug HUD.

nodes.name: _areBlocksEqual
nodes.summary: Compares two block lists with tolerance to short-circuit redundant structure updates when DOM has not meaningfully changed.

nodes.name: gestalt-processor.js
nodes.summary: Runs DBSCAN spatial clustering and bounding-box merging on DOM blocks to produce Gestalt-grouped regions used by the V1/V4 stage for proximity-based perceptual grouping.
nodes.languageNotes: Custom DBSCAN with Chebyshev distance over block centroids; merges overlapping cluster bounding boxes iteratively.

nodes.name: GestaltProcessor
nodes.summary: DBSCAN-based clusterer that groups DOM blocks into perceptual regions and merges their bounding boxes for downstream rendering.

nodes.name: primitive-map.js
nodes.summary: Maintains an RGBA8 canvas encoding per-pixel V4 primitive attributes (e.g., text density, color flags) for upload to the foveated WebGL pipeline.

nodes.name: PrimitiveMap
nodes.summary: Manages a downscaled ImageData canvas storing encoded primitive properties drawn as axis-aligned blocks for GPU sampling.

nodes.name: primitive-meta.js
nodes.summary: Companion canvas for primitive metadata flags (e.g., text-bearing, link, image type) encoded as U8 channels for V4 shader lookup.

nodes.name: PrimitiveMeta
nodes.summary: Tracks per-block metadata flags on a U8-encoded canvas, paralleling PrimitiveMap for richer shader-side classification.

nodes.name: structure-map.js
nodes.summary: Lower-resolution structure canvas encoding coarse DOM block boundaries used to modulate peripheral rendering and reading-band detection.

nodes.name: StructureMap
nodes.summary: Maintains the coarse structure ImageData canvas, encoding block bounds per pixel for the foveated shader.

nodes.name: dom-aware-draw-order.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest unit tests verifying that DOM-aware draw order paints non-text-bearing primitives before text-bearing ones, preserving text visibility in primitive/meta maps.

nodes.name: primitive-map.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest unit tests validating PrimitiveMap encoding, resize, clear, and drawBlock pixel-level correctness with a stubbed document/canvas.

nodes.name: primitive-meta.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest unit tests covering PrimitiveMeta U8 encoding, resize, and metadata flag drawBlock behavior with a stub canvas.

nodes.name: crawler.js
nodes.summary: Playwright-based parallel page crawler that visits URLs across multiple viewports and scroll positions, capturing PNG screenshots for downstream perceptual analysis.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses worker-pool concurrency pattern with shared queue plus async IIFE workers.

nodes.name: capturePages
nodes.summary: Launches a Chromium browser and dispatches URLs across a pool of concurrent workers, capturing PNGs for each viewport-scroll combination with per-page error isolation.

nodes.name: reporter.js
nodes.summary: Aggregates per-page perceptual analyses into structured reports and renders them as console tables, JSON, or styled HTML with color-coded score columns.

nodes.name: buildReport
nodes.summary: Flattens raw page captures into a normalized report object with min/max/mean aggregates over scores, congestion, and edge density.

nodes.name: printTable
nodes.summary: Renders a report as an ASCII console.table with truncated URLs and rating summaries for terminal viewing.

nodes.name: writeReport
nodes.summary: Persists a report to disk as JSON or HTML based on the output file extension.

nodes.name: buildHtmlReport
nodes.summary: Generates a self-contained HTML report with inline CSS and a color-graded score table, escaping URLs and error strings for safe rendering.

nodes.name: buildComparisonReport
nodes.summary: Diffs two reports by joining captures across URL/viewport/scroll-position and producing per-cell score deltas for before/after comparisons.

nodes.name: scroll-strategy.js
nodes.summary: Defines named scroll positions (top, mid, bottom) with page evaluation functions and resolves comma-separated CLI inputs into the corresponding strategy objects.

nodes.name: sitemap-parser.js
nodes.summary: Lightweight sitemap.xml fetcher using Node's built-in http/https modules with redirect following and regex-based <loc> extraction (no XML parser dependency).

nodes.name: url-resolver.js
nodes.summary: Resolves heterogeneous URL sources (raw URLs, local text files, sitemap URLs) into a deduplicated, normalized URL list ready for the crawler.

nodes.name: viewport-profiles.js
nodes.summary: Catalog of named viewport profiles (desktop, mobile, tablet) with device characteristics and a resolver that maps comma-separated CLI input to profile objects.

nodes.name: scrutinizer-audit.js
nodes.summary: End-to-end CLI entry point that orchestrates URL resolution, headless crawling, perceptual analysis, and report generation for batch website audits.

nodes.name: parseArgs
nodes.summary: Parses CLI argv into an options object supporting URLs, sitemap sources, viewport/scroll selectors, output paths, and comparison mode.

nodes.name: printHelp
nodes.summary: Prints the CLI usage text with available flags, viewport names, and example invocations.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Top-level async orchestrator that resolves URLs, runs the crawler, invokes the analyzer per capture, optionally saves heatmap PNGs, then writes table/JSON/HTML reports.

nodes.name: urlToSlug
nodes.summary: Converts a URL into a filesystem-safe slug for use in output filenames.

nodes.name: main.js
nodes.summary: Electron main process entry point that creates the Scrutinizer overlay/content windows, wires IPC, builds menus, runs test/batch capture modes, and handles auto-updates and web calibration.
nodes.languageNotes: CommonJS Electron main with extensive IPC surface area; mixes window lifecycle, menu rebuild, mobile UA emulation, integration test runner, and batch capture pipeline in a single ~3k LOC module.

nodes.name: sendToRenderer
nodes.summary: Forwards an IPC message to the main renderer (overlay window) if its webContents are alive.

nodes.name: sendToOverlays
nodes.summary: Broadcasts an IPC message to all overlay windows, skipping any with destroyed webContents.

nodes.name: rebuildMenu
nodes.summary: Reconstructs the application menu from the current settings so menu-driven toggles reflect live state.

nodes.name: applyMobileEmulation
nodes.summary: Applies mobile device emulation (user-agent, viewport, touch) to a webContents target so SERPs and pages can be captured as mobile.

nodes.name: canNavigate
nodes.summary: Gate that decides whether a navigation event is permitted, used to constrain the embedded browser.

nodes.name: createScrutinizerWindow
nodes.summary: Primary window factory that creates the overlay BrowserWindow plus the underlying content view, wires every IPC handler, and installs lifecycle/menu/preference behavior.

nodes.name: createSplashWindow
nodes.summary: Creates a small frameless splash window shown during app boot.

nodes.name: createWindow
nodes.summary: Top-level window bootstrap that decides between splash, main Scrutinizer window, and test/batch modes based on CLI flags.

nodes.name: runTestMode
nodes.summary: Headless test entry that opens a window for a single URL and exits, used by smoke and CI checks.

nodes.name: runIntegrationTest
nodes.summary: Large integration-test driver that exercises the full Scrutinizer pipeline across modes, parameters, and pages, asserting renderer state via IPC.
nodes.languageNotes: Nearly 1k LOC of scripted IPC choreography — effectively an in-process E2E harness.

nodes.name: runBatchCapture
nodes.summary: Runs batched headless captures over a list of URLs/modes, writing PNGs with embedded citation metadata for research datasets.

nodes.name: setupAutoUpdater
nodes.summary: Configures electron-updater event handlers (download progress, errors, restart prompts) for the production build.

nodes.name: checkForAppUpdates
nodes.summary: Manually triggers an update check via electron-updater and reports the outcome through dialogs.

nodes.name: startWebCalibration
nodes.summary: Launches the external web-based foveal calibration flow (scrutinizer-www) and listens for completion postMessages.

nodes.name: handleCalibrationComplete
nodes.summary: Receives calibration results from the web flow, persists derived radius/ppd settings, and rebuilds menus to reflect the new values.

nodes.name: menu-template.js
nodes.summary: Defines the full Electron application menu (modes, parameters, debug toggles, capture/export, help) as a single large factory consumed by main.js.
nodes.languageNotes: Single ~1k-line factory function returning a Menu template; complexity is breadth (many submenus) rather than depth.

nodes.name: buildMenuTemplate
nodes.summary: Builds the full Electron menu template from current settings, wiring every menu item to the matching IPC/main-process handler.

nodes.name: citation-export.js
nodes.summary: Embeds and extracts Scrutinizer experiment metadata (version, mode, fovea parameters, citation) in PNG tEXt chunks for reproducible academic exports.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses pngjs to round-trip tEXt chunks; also writes a JSON sidecar so consumers without PNG parsers still get the metadata.

nodes.name: generateCitation
nodes.summary: Composes a human-readable citation string from version, mode label, and timestamp.

nodes.name: buildMetadata
nodes.summary: Assembles the full metadata key/value map from current renderer state, including mode info, fovea geometry, and pipeline configuration.

nodes.name: embedMetadata
nodes.summary: Reads a PNG buffer, injects metadata into tEXt chunks, and returns the annotated buffer.

nodes.name: extractMetadata
nodes.summary: Parses a PNG file and returns the Scrutinizer metadata stored in its tEXt chunks.

nodes.name: saveWithMetadata
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that embeds metadata and writes the annotated PNG to disk.

nodes.name: generateSidecar
nodes.summary: Writes a JSON sidecar alongside an exported PNG containing the same citation metadata for tools that cannot read PNG tEXt.

nodes.name: config.js
nodes.summary: Central renderer-side defaults for the Scrutinizer effect — foveal geometry, blur/desaturation strength, fixation thresholds, DoG/peripheral reconstruction toggles, debug flags.
nodes.languageNotes: Dual-mode module: a global CONFIG object for browser use and a CommonJS export (DEFAULT_SETTINGS, CALIBRATION_URL) for the main process.

nodes.name: overlay.js
nodes.summary: Renderer entry for the HUD overlay window — instantiates the Scrutinizer engine, bridges browser-view mouse/scroll events over IPC, and forwards renderer logs to the main process.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what Scrutinizer is: a foveated vision simulator that models human peripheral vision in three biological stages (LGN, V1, V4) and binds the simulated fovea to the mouse cursor. The README describes the architecture, install paths, keyboard shortcuts, and the psychophysical validation strategy. Treat it as the map for the rest of the tour — every later step drills into a component named here.

tour.title: Electron Main Process
tour.description: main.js is the Electron entry point and by far the highest fan-out node in the graph (21 outgoing edges). It creates the overlay and content windows, wires IPC between processes, builds the menu, drives test/batch capture modes used by the validation scripts, and handles auto-updates plus web calibration. Reading it gives you a bird's-eye view of how the desktop app, the headless capture pipeline, and the calibration flow all share one runtime.
tour.languageLesson: Electron splits into a Node.js main process (main.js) and one or more Chromium renderer processes. The main process owns OS-level concerns (windows, menus, file dialogs, IPC), while renderers run the web UI. They communicate via ipcMain/ipcRenderer message channels — never by sharing memory directly.

tour.title: Renderer Bootstrap
tour.description: renderer/app.js is the top-level bootstrap inside the Electron window. It wires together the Scrutinizer visualizer, the toolbar, and the DOM adapter so the rest of the renderer can assume those collaborators exist. Think of it as the renderer-side counterpart to main.js from Step 2: short, declarative, and the single place where the foveated pipeline gets handed real DOM and canvas references.

tour.title: The Foveated Render Loop
tour.description: renderer/scrutinizer.js is the orchestrator at the heart of the project. It owns the per-frame render loop and glues together gaze tracking, content analysis, the WebGL and WebGPU pipelines, the SVG overlay, visual memory, and IPC. Every later step in the tour describes a subsystem that this file coordinates. The WebGL 2 visualizer it drives uploads textures, links the peripheral shader program, and issues the actual GPU draw calls.
tour.languageLesson: WebGL 2 programs use GLSL ES 3.0 shaders. Textures are uploaded once per frame from CPU-prepared canvases (structure map, saliency map, primitive map) and sampled by a fragment shader that applies eccentricity-dependent pooling. The CPU's job is to prepare clean inputs; the GPU's job is to apply the falloff.

tour.title: LGN Stage — DOM Structure & Saliency
tour.description: The LGN stage in Scrutinizer is implemented as DOM-aware content analysis: renderer/content-analysis.js coordinates the saliency and congestion Web Workers, manages structure/primitive/meta canvases, and runs Gestalt clustering before uploading texture maps to the renderer. renderer/dom-primitive-classifier.js feeds it by classifying each DOM node into a coarse rendering primitive — text, image, button, panel — so the model can suppress blank areas and boost important regions just like a biological relay/gating stage.

tour.title: V1 Stage — Feature Congestion
tour.description: The V1 stage models cortical detail: 12 half-octave DoG bands plus density-gated crowding. renderer/congestion-core.js is the pure-JS heart of that math — separable Gaussian blur, local variance, Sobel-like edge density, normalization, and the composite Feature Congestion score (0–100) that the headless CLI also consumes. Pure-JS placement is deliberate: the same code path runs in the renderer for real-time feedback and in Node for offline scoring.
tour.languageLesson: Feature Congestion (Rosenholtz et al.) approximates how much a region taxes peripheral processing. It combines color variance, contrast, and edge density into a single scalar. Half-octave Difference-of-Gaussians (DoG) bands are a classic V1 model: each band responds to a narrow range of spatial frequencies, mimicking simple-cell tuning.

tour.title: V4 Stage — Color & Calibration
tour.description: The V4 stage handles per-channel chromatic decay — red-green fades before blue-yellow in periphery — and couples that with the spatial pooling from V1. renderer/oklab-utils.js provides the perceptually uniform color space (Oklab forward/inverse + desaturation by chroma scaling) that makes the chromatic falloff principled rather than ad-hoc. renderer/peripheral-calibration.js anchors the whole pipeline to the user's actual foveal extent by estimating peripheral pixels-per-degree from on-screen calibration markers.
tour.languageLesson: Oklab is a perceptually uniform color space designed so Euclidean distance approximates perceived color difference. Working in Oklab means a 'desaturate by 30%' operation behaves the same regardless of hue — critical when modeling chromatic decay where naive RGB desaturation would shift apparent hue.

tour.title: Overlays, HUD & Visual Feedback
tour.description: On top of the foveated render, two overlay subsystems show what the model is doing. renderer/svg-overlay.js draws fovea/parafovea rings, comfort guides, tick marks, an optional grid, and the cursor indicator above the WebGL canvas. renderer/complexity-hud.js is a draggable HUD that visualizes per-frame visual complexity scores, regional crowding/edge stats, and pipeline performance across tabbed views — essentially a live diagnostic surface for the LGN/V1/V4 stages from Steps 5–7.

tour.title: Headless CLI & MCP Server
tour.description: The same vision model also runs without a UI. cli/scrutinizer-audit.js is the end-to-end CLI: URL resolution, headless crawling, perceptual analysis, and report generation for batch website audits. cli/mcp/server.js exposes that pipeline over the Model Context Protocol so an LLM agent can score visual congestion of any live URL via Playwright. This is how the renderer's congestion-core (Step 6) becomes an analyzer other tools can call.
tour.languageLesson: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a JSON-RPC style protocol that lets LLM agents call typed tools on external servers. A tool is declared with a name, input schema, and handler. The server here wraps Playwright captures + congestion scoring as tools an agent can invoke conversationally.

tour.title: Validation Harness
tour.description: Because the model makes empirical claims about peripheral vision, validation is first-class. scripts/lib/capture-runner.js (fan-in 9, second only to package.json) is the shared engine that batches Electron child processes to capture rendered output. scripts/validate-isotropic-rendering.js runs five checks against those captures — angular isotropy, readability destruction, texture preservation, dark-mode scatter, mode comparison — so regressions in the LGN/V1/V4 math are caught before release.

tour.title: The Vision Model on Paper
tour.description: The code in Steps 4–7 implements ideas that are documented as living specs. docs/foveated-vision-model.md is the definitive reference for the biology, coordinate system, three spatial zones, strength masks, domain warping, mipmap crowding, and the universal structure-map pipeline. docs/specs/implemented/isotropic_cortical_sampling.md captures the FOVI-derived isotropic sector geometry now shipped as the default V1 sampling mode, verified against Blauch's Python implementation. docs/validation-journal.md (fan-in 6) is the running log that ties code changes to perceptual outcomes.
